zh: 某类商品现在出售能得到它当前的剩余件数，之后同类商品的价格只会越来越低；所以每一次出售都希望拿到当前所有类别中最高的价格。
采用贪心策略，每次都卖当前剩余件数最多的那一类。交换论证说明，先卖库存较大的类别不会让总收入变少。
用最大堆存放各类的剩余件数，重复m次：弹出最大值q，收入加q，若q>1则把q−1放回堆。总收入最多约10^10，使用64位整数。
en: Selling an item of a category now earns its current remaining count, and later prices in that category only go down, so every sale should take the highest current price among all categories.
Use a greedy rule and always sell from the category with the most items left. An exchange argument shows that selling from the larger stock first never reduces the total revenue.
Keep the remaining counts in a max-heap and repeat m times: pop the maximum q, add q to the revenue, and push q−1 back if q>1. The revenue is at most about 10^10, so use 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Use a max-heap to maintain the current remaining quantity of each category. Each time, pop the maximum value q and add q to the revenue; after the sale, if q>1, push q−1 back onto the heap. Repeat exactly m times.

Under the optimal rule, the first six prices in source example one are 10, 10, 9, 9, 9, 8, totaling 55; in example two the prices are 4, 3, 2, 2, totaling 11. Both match the source outputs.

The original constraints do not state a lower bound on the total stock, but "selling exactly m items" requires a feasible input, so this site makes the necessary condition `m ≤ sum(quantity)` explicit as the valid input domain. This condition does not prescribe any behavior when stock is insufficient, and it does not change the meaning of the problem on feasible inputs.

## Correctness

If a category whose current stock is q is sold now, it earns q immediately; afterwards the prices obtainable from that category only decrease. If an optimal plan does not first pick the category with the largest current stock but a category with a smaller stock, swap the order of the two categories' first picks: selling the larger stock first gives an immediate gain that is no lower, and its subsequent decreasing sequence is term by term no lower than the smaller stock's sequence, so the swap does not reduce the total revenue. Equivalently, choosing the largest current price at every step has the greedy-choice property. Selling and pushing q−1 back onto the heap exactly represents the stock at the next moment, and induction shows that the total revenue is maximal.

## Complexity

Heap initialization is O(n), and each sale does at most one pop and one push, so the time is O(n + m log n) and the space is O(n). The maximum revenue does not exceed 10^10, so 64-bit integers are sufficient.
